items.title: Ray Bauduc Interview, 1984-06-27
items.q: So, I gave him this whole set of drums, I brought them all down there. I mean, I, the, the guy was kissing me and everything, he was so happy.

ctx.x: That's when Baby Dots was playing on, and then, uh, well, when we'd get through at the, in fact, tell me about, about that thing. When we was playing at the Blackhawk, the second time, the second time that we played the Blackhawk, I'd been, I'd been working, the first time I went on that, I was working with the drum factory, designing drums and stuff, so you'd get the new drums and all. Mm-hmm. So, in the meantime, when we left New York, after we got, I left Pollock's band, I had a set of drums that Pollock, I, I…
But, did you see Paul much in Chicago?

items.title: Ray Bauduc Interview, 1984-06-26
items.q: Well, Baby Dodge... He played with... What Fade Merrill was banned

ctx.x: Well, how did Baby Dodge rate in those days? When you were down in New Orleans?

Well, Baby Dodge... He played with... What Fade Merrill was banned before Zutty and those guys... Played on... On the Sidney. Mm-hmm. When Louis Armstrong played with the band, you know? Mm-hmm. And he... He played... New Orleans drums. I don't know whether he could read or not. I mean...

items.title: Ray Bauduc and Nappy Lamare Interview, 1959-09-09
items.q: Well, Baby Dots and Zootie Singleton.

ctx.x: Who were your favorite drummers when you were a kid that you listened to?
Well, Baby Dots and Zootie Singleton. And there was another drummer that came down with... What's that name? Faith Marlowe's band that was on the... Oh, yeah.
You mentioned the other night you couldn't think of the name.
